core.title: The documentation-graph resolver lives in the owning extension
core.when: You plan where the resolver code lives.
core.then: The resolver MUST live in the extension that owns the documentation graph.
avoid: Placing the resolver in a shared utility module outside the owning extension.
core.why: Spec 2 §5.4 places the resolver in the owning extension.
evidence: The resolver's code is located inside the owning extension's module.
verification: Strict disposition at severity 1: every finding fails the run; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

A validator checks that the resolver's code is located inside the owning extension's module (the placement required by spec 2 §5.4); the validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details.
Observing the change facts (resolver source changed / resolver moved) needs a new observer with a path mapping for the owning extension, taken from the profile.

fires: A plan puts the resolver in a shared utility module outside the owning extension.
doesNotFire: Pure markup authoring with no resolver work.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the extension that owns the documentation graph lives, so that 'the resolver lives in the owning extension' is checkable and so the change observer can map resolver source changes and moves.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the docs extension — the extension that owns the docs-graph resolver; its path mapping is needed by the change observer

profileRequirements.meaning: The markup file suffixes of the documentation corpus, so that 'pure markup authoring' names the realization's authored documents.

proposedKeys.meaning: Directory of one extension — a self-contained capability module — used to check that the extension's dedicated code lives inside it and to map changes to it.
proposedKeys.bunValue: the docs extension (owns the docs-graph resolver)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The roles group lists only architectural layer and test roles, and the layout group covers wagon, feature, commons, plan and test locations; no existing key says where a capability extension's module lives.

bunOnly.reason: It names the realization's concrete shared-utility package; the neutral core keeps only stack-neutral task terms and the Bun realization restores this one for plan-text matching.
The validator id and shared-policy reference id of this one rule are realization details; the core's verification describes the check generically.

classification.note: 'The docs-graph resolver' is restated as the documentation-graph resolver; no stack content.
One obligation: placement in the owning extension; which extension owns the graph comes from the profile.

'A shared package outside the docs extension' becomes a shared utility module outside the owning extension.
Observable restatement: resolver code inside the owning extension's module.

Three task terms are neutral and stay in the core; 'coach utils' names the realization's shared-utility package and is bunOnly.
Change values are neutral event names; the fact's note ('needs a path mapping for the docs extension') is satisfied by the profile key.
'Shared utility package outside the docs extension' neutralized to shared utility module outside the owning extension.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is placement/ownership, so it neutralizes cleanly: the resolver lives in the extension that owns the graph, never in a shared utility module. Two things could not be neutral: (1) which extension owns the graph and where it lives — no vocabulary key exists, so layout.extension_dir is proposed and referenced by then/avoid/evidence/verification and the change observer; (2) the task term 'coach utils' and the validator ref 'docs_capability' name realization specifics and stay bunOnly. 'Spec 2 §5.4' is a convention-level citation, not a stack artifact, and is kept verbatim. The '.adoc' suffix in doesNotFire is reconstructed from suffix.markup. The 'additions' block of bun.json is rewrite provenance, not an obligation, so it is not classified.
